A light review: only the changed hunks are in scope, which are rail.tsx's one added attribute, use-media-query.ts's internals, and two statements in first-run.tsx's handler. This is the rule the change exists to satisfy, and it was being broken. Rail renders role="progressbar", which makes it a control to assistive technology, and its required label prop reached only aria-valuetext — the *value*, not the name. So the bar had no accessible name at all: a screen reader announced "62% of food" with nothing saying what the 62% was of. rail.tsx:29 now sets aria-label={label}. Proven rather than asserted: rail.test.tsx queries getByRole('progressbar', {name: 'Food and groceries'}), and removing the attribute fails that one case and only that case.

A light review: only the changed hunks are in scope, which are rail.tsx's one added attribute, use-media-query.ts's internals, and two statements in first-run.tsx's handler. No information is shown by colour alone, and the hunk improves this too. Rail's tone picks a fill colour — emerald, ochre, rose or slate — and the proportion it encodes is also carried as text in aria-valuetext and, as of this change, named by aria-label. So a person who cannot distinguish the tones still gets the figure and what it belongs to. The tone values themselves are untouched.

Checked by computing it from the tokens rather than deferred for want of a browser, which is possible because contrast is arithmetic on the values and both themes declare theirs in apps/web/src/design/tokens.css. Rail's fill against its own track is a user interface component boundary, so WCAG 2.1 success criterion 1.4.11 applies and the bar is 3:1. Computed with the WCAG relative-luminance formula for all four tones in both themes: light emerald #0f5c3c on track #ede7da 6.51:1, ochre #8c5c15 4.66:1, slate #3c4a5a 7.35:1, rose #9e2b2b 6.01:1; dark emerald #4ecb8b on track #1a2129 7.92:1, ochre #e5a93f 7.79:1, slate #8fa7c0 6.54:1, rose #f0736b 5.70:1. All eight pass, the worst being light ochre at 4.66:1, comfortably above 3:1 and above 4.5:1 as well. Nothing in this change alters a token or a fill, so these are the ratios before and after it.

summary: Incomplete, not fail: nothing is wrong, but DES-13 could not be checked. DES-08 was being broken and is fixed — Rail's progressbar had no accessible name at all, since its label reached aria-valuetext, the value, rather than the name. A screen reader said '62% of food' with nothing saying what of. Proven by a test that fails when the attribute is removed. Contrast needs the rendered screen, which this review cannot see, and no colour changed.
